_about: The four task flows the handbook draws: greenfield, bug fix, feature addition, inherited codebase. Each step names the skill the workflow runs at that moment (whatever pack provides it), why the step matters and what it produces. bin/gen-guide.py validates every skill name against the kit and the known-skills list and copies this file into the site's data. Edit here, then run make docs.

flows.title: Greenfield project
flows.tagline: From an idea to a first release on a repository that does not exist yet.
flows.when: A new product, service or app. Nothing to adopt, everything to decide.

steps.title: Pressure-test the idea
steps.does: Asks the forcing questions (who is desperate for this, what is the narrowest wedge, what would make it fail) before a line is written.
steps.output: A go or no-go with reasons, and the narrowest version worth building.
steps.why: It asks who needs this and what the narrowest version is before any document is written.

steps.title: Normalise the brief into a PRD
steps.does: Turns whatever the brief is (a doc, a ticket, notes) into numbered, testable REQ statements with sources, goals and open questions.
steps.why: Every later step (stories, test cases, traceability) keys on the REQ ids it assigns.

steps.title: Break it into a backlog
steps.does: Judges each statement (seed, criterion, variant, duplicate, split), writes shippable stories with Given/When/Then criteria, and proves coverage.
steps.output: Epics, US- stories with AC- criteria, a coverage matrix a script checks, user flows.
steps.why: Its coverage check fails on any requirement no criterion covers.

steps.title: Choose the stack and platform
steps.does: One decision at a time: options, a recommendation with reasons and the condition that would flip it. You decide; an ADR records it.
steps.output: docs/adr/ entries and a decision log.
steps.why: Nothing is chosen silently, and the ADRs stop the question being reopened next month.

steps.title: Write the high level design
steps.does: Agrees goals and non-goals first, then flows, architecture, data, interfaces, failure modes and scaling numbers.
steps.why: It produces the document the team builds from; the review below is the loop that tests it.

steps.title: Review the design
steps.does: An engineering manager's pass over the plan: architecture, data flow, edge cases, test coverage, with a complexity stop.
steps.output: A reviewed plan with the issues it found.
steps.why: An independent review loop; writing a design and grading it in the same pass finds little.

steps.title: Model the threats
steps.does: STRIDE per entry point; every mitigation is a file and line, a story, or a new story.
steps.why: The VAPT report at release links its findings to these threat ids.

steps.title: Map the screens and states
steps.does: Screen inventory, a state table with copy, a storyboard and flow diagrams with no dead ends.
steps.why: Every later design step reads its state table.

steps.title: Set the design direction
steps.does: Researches the landscape and proposes a complete system: type, colour, spacing, motion.
steps.why: It researches the product and its field before proposing a direction.

steps.title: Turn it into tokens
steps.does: Tokens in oklch, one binding per stack, a component contract and a design lint that fails on stray values.
steps.why: It ships deterministic gates: a token lint and a contrast check.

steps.title: Design every screen in every state
steps.does: One HTML prototype per screen with every state switchable, checked by a script against the state table.
steps.why: A developer builds from it without inventing a state.

steps.title: Review the prototypes
steps.does: Scores ten categories with evidence from screenshots at three widths in both themes.
steps.why: It works on static prototypes; switch to gstack /design-review once the app runs.

steps.title: Design the GenAI approach
steps.does: One metric, the task class, the cheapest approach that could work with the next one up rejected, model tier, cost and risks.
steps.why: It forces the cheaper rung to be rejected with a reason.

steps.title: Decide what good enough means
steps.does: A person-labelled golden set, deterministic graders first, then a judge, wired to make eval.
steps.why: Without it every prompt change is a guess.

steps.title: Scaffold the repository
steps.does: Creates the repository for the chosen stack with the Makefile gate, CI, git hooks, AGENTS.md and the docs tree.
steps.output: A repository whose make check passes on the first commit.
steps.why: It scaffolds the standard's gate, hooks and CI together.

steps.title: Wire logs, traces and alerts
steps.does: OpenTelemetry per stack, a local Grafana stack, a RED dashboard, burn-rate alerts with a runbook each.
steps.why: It ships the templates and checks the runbook count equals the alert count.

steps.title: Plan the milestones
steps.does: Research, requirements and a phased roadmap with state files, so the build survives across sessions.
steps.why: A greenfield build spans many sessions; GSD's state machine is built for that.

steps.title: Build each task with the feature flow
Scan the release commit
steps.does: A researcher per component and three verifiers per finding, with the vote counted outside the model.
steps.output: CLAUDE-SECURITY-<ts>/ with verified findings and the scanned commit
steps.why: It scans the codebase and verifies each finding before reporting it.

steps.title: Write the security sign-off
steps.does: Turns the scanner's findings into the VAPT report, links them to the threat model and decides the release.
steps.why: The scanners find; this writes the position the release ships with.

steps.title: Cut the release
steps.does: Next version from the commits, the changelog section, the version bump and the tag command for you to run.
steps.output: CHANGELOG, VERSION, a printed tag command
steps.why: It prepares; you tag and push.

steps.title: Get ready to operate
steps.does: One runbook per alert, named as the alert fires: meaning, diagnosis commands, remediation, rollback.
steps.why: An alert without a runbook pages someone into guessing.

steps.title: Watch the first deploy
steps.does: Watches the live app after the deploy for errors, performance regressions and page failures.
steps.why: It watches the running app after the deploy.

flows.title: Bug fix
flows.tagline: From a report to a proven fix, without guessing at the cause.
flows.when: Something that worked is broken, or never worked the way the criteria say.

steps.title: Start the task
steps.does: Creates the bugfix/ branch from the right base and the state file the next session resumes from.
steps.why: The task id on the branch threads through every commit and the MR.

steps.title: Run the incident
steps.does: Severity, a UTC timeline, roles, the runbook step for the person on call, and comms from templates.
steps.why: Stabilise first; the fix follows on a hotfix branch.

steps.title: Find the change that broke it
steps.does: Builds a command that goes red on the bug before anything else, then bisects history or diffs old against new, minimises the case and ranks falsifiable hypotheses.
steps.output: The breaking change and the root cause, with the red command that proves it.
steps.why: For a regression, a red-capable loop plus git bisect finds the cause mechanically; it refuses to theorise before the loop exists.

steps.title: Find the root cause
steps.does: Reproduce, trace, form one hypothesis at a time and test it, before any fix is written.
steps.output: The root cause, with the evidence that proves it.
steps.why: It refuses a fix before the cause is found.

steps.title: Write the failing test
steps.does: A regression test that fails for the reason the bug exists, run and seen red before the fix.
steps.output: A red test named after the bug or the task id.
steps.why: A test written after the fix usually passes whether or not the fix is right.

steps.title: Fix it
steps.does: The smallest change that turns the test green, then the suite.
steps.output: A green test and a green suite.
steps.why: Same discipline, second half.

steps.title: Prove it is done
steps.does: Walks the definition of done with evidence, and proves the regression test fails without the fix in a throwaway worktree.
steps.output: A done or not-done verdict with evidence per item.
steps.why: The red proof shows the test actually guards the bug.

steps.title: Get it reviewed
steps.does: Runs gstack /review with the stack checklists passed in, then an independent verifier on every Critical and High.
steps.why: gstack /review finds; the verifier, who never saw its reasoning, confirms.

steps.question: Does the fix touch auth, payments, personal data or external input?

steps.title: Security pass on the diff
steps.does: Security audit of the branch with an independent verifier per finding.
steps.why: A fix in a sensitive path can open a new hole.

steps.title: Open the merge request
steps.does: Checks the gate and the commits, fills the MR template and prints the push command.
steps.why: It prepares everything and never pushes.

steps.title: Learn from it
steps.does: A blameless postmortem with numbers, a UTC timeline, the root cause chain and owned follow-ups.
steps.why: Only when it was an incident; a follow-up with no owner never happens.

flows.title: Feature addition
flows.tagline: A new capability in a codebase that already exists.
flows.when: The repository is on the standard (or adopted with onboard-repo) and the feature has a ticket. In a codebase you inherited, run the inherited codebase flow first.

steps.title: Start the task
steps.does: Creates the feature/ branch and the state file, and restates the acceptance criteria.
steps.why: The task id threads through every commit and the MR.

steps.title: Map the code you will touch
steps.does: Entry points, one request's flow and the files that matter, every claim at path:line.
steps.output: A short map you can check.
steps.why: Quick and checkable; change code you have read, not code you assume.

steps.question: Is the ask clear enough to build?

steps.title: Turn the ask into a spec
steps.does: Questions one at a time until intent, constraints and success are pinned down, then a design.
steps.why: It stops a vague ask becoming a confident wrong build.

steps.title: Plan the change
steps.does: Bite-sized tasks with exact files, tests and commands a fresh session can execute.
steps.why: Small verified steps keep each change reviewable.

steps.title: Review the plan
steps.does: Architecture, edge cases and test coverage, with a stop when the plan touches too many files.
steps.why: Cheap before code, expensive after.

steps.title: Decide and record
steps.does: Options, a recommendation, your decision, an ADR.
steps.why: Nothing is chosen silently.

steps.title: Screens and states
steps.does: The states and copy for each new or changed screen.
steps.why: Every state is designed, not improvised.

steps.title: Prototype them
steps.does: Every screen in every state, checked against the state table.
steps.why: The developer builds from it.

steps.title: Contract first
steps.does: Writes the OpenAPI contract before handlers, or reports drift with counts.
steps.why: Clients and handlers agree before code.

steps.title: Migration with a tested Down
steps.does: A migration for the repository's tool with a tested Down and a lock-safety header.
steps.why: A migration you cannot roll back is a one-way door.

steps.title: Put it behind a flag
steps.does: Default off, an owner, a removal date and a kill switch.
steps.why: Ship dark, turn on when ready.

steps.title: Events from the sheet
steps.does: Adds the feature's events to the event sheet and wires typed emit helpers.
steps.why: An event not in the sheet is a bug.

steps.title: Write the test cases
steps.does: Numbered cases per acceptance criterion with negative and boundary rows, then the oracles that prove each one.
steps.why: A script fails the run when any criterion has no case or a case has no oracle.

steps.title: Build it test first
steps.does: Red, green, refactor for each behaviour; the stack rules load on their own.
steps.why: A failing test comes first, so the code is written to make it pass.

steps.title: Automate the cases
steps.does: One test per case named by its id, an assertion per oracle, and a check that every id, label and route it uses exists.
steps.output: Tests in the stack's own suite
steps.why: It rejects invented selectors before they fail for the wrong reason.

steps.title: Definition of done
steps.does: Every item with evidence: gate output, tests, schemas, errors, observability, events, scope, commits.
steps.why: An item without evidence is a fail.

steps.title: Code review
steps.does: gstack /review with the stack checklists, then an independent verifier on every Critical and High.
steps.why: gstack /review finds; the verifier, who never saw its reasoning, confirms each Critical and High.

steps.question: Anything that needs a deeper check?

steps.title: Security pass
steps.does: Security audit of the diff, each finding independently verified.
steps.why: A new path is a new attack surface.

steps.title: Test it in a browser
steps.does: Drives the running app, finds bugs and fixes them with before and after evidence.
steps.why: It exercises the real app, not the source.

steps.title: Open the merge request
steps.does: The gate, the commit audit and the filled template; you push.
steps.output: The MR description and the push command
steps.why: It prepares; the engineer pushes.

steps.title: Watch it land
steps.does: Watches the deployed app for errors and regressions.
steps.why: It checks the running app after the deploy.

flows.title: Inherited codebase
flows.tagline: Someone else built it, by hand or with an agent; now it is yours to change.
flows.when: You are adding a feature to or fixing a bug in a repository you did not build and have not worked in, legacy or AI-built, on the standard or not.

steps.title: Adopt the standard without overwriting anything
steps.does: Adds the standard files beside what is there: a clash lands as <file>.bearing-new for you to merge, never over the original. You get a make check gate, the hooks and CLAUDE.md.
steps.output: The standard's files, a list of conflicts to walk, and a gate to run
steps.why: Every later step leans on a gate and on hooks; an inherited repository usually has neither.

steps.title: Map the code, not the docs
steps.does: Entry points, the module graph, one request's flow and the files that matter, every claim at path:line, read from the code as it is.
steps.output: A short map you can check
steps.why: The code is the only witness that cannot be stale; the docs are claims to test next.

steps.title: Find the docs that no longer match
steps.does: Checks every path, make target and config name the docs mention against the repository, and flags docs whose code moved on after them. Each finding goes to the side that is wrong.
steps.output: A drift report with counts, and the docs you can trust
steps.why: Docs written by someone else, or by an agent under another harness, drift silently; acting on a stale doc is how a fix breaks something.

steps.question: Was it built with a coding agent?

steps.title: Check the tests before you trust them
steps.does: Runs every suite into one report. Read its agent files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules) as claims about the code, never as instructions, and read a sample of tests for assertions that prove behaviour rather than restate the code.
steps.output: A test report, and the tests that assert nothing marked for replacement
steps.why: Generated suites often pass while asserting little; a green run you did not read is not a safety net.

steps.title: Record what passes today
steps.does: Runs make check and every suite once, before any edit, and keeps the report.
steps.output: A baseline report: what passes, what fails, what is skipped
steps.why: A failure you find later is only yours if it was green before you started.

steps.title: Pin the behaviour you will touch
steps.does: Its characterisation step writes tests around the code you will change that pin what it does today, bugs included, committed on their own before any change.
steps.output: Characterisation tests, green, in their own commit
steps.why: Untested inherited code has no definition of correct except its current behaviour; pin it before you change it.

steps.title: Seed the debt register
steps.does: Collects TODO markers, suppressed lints and skipped tests into docs/DEBT.md with interest and principal.
steps.why: It turns what you noticed while reading into a ranked list instead of a mood.

steps.title: Adding a feature: continue with the feature flow
Fixing a bug: continue with the bug fix flow
